features: One continuous upright central green stem rises from large orange-brown swollen tapering root with fine lateral root hairs.
Several long arched/lax side axes carry separate pointed triangular or arrow-like green blades with basal notches and some irregular lobes.
Multiple hanging clusters of small circular outlined bodies with red centres occur at ends of the lateral axes. These are fruit-like drawing structures, not an identified species.
Root broadens below stem and tapers sideways to a point; body is mostly a smooth outlined mass with drawn internal strokes and fine protruding fibres.
herbal_anatomy.limits: No species identification, organ translation, glyph reading, or botanical life-cycle claim. Whole depicted anatomy does not prove a botanically exhaustive plant.

limits: Historical development nominations are not independent holdouts.
Source-nominated identity is a hypothesis, not ground truth.
No ROOT, q, Part operator, species, process or extraction translation.
No GDT388 gate or reserved-confirmation claim.
Whole-canvas incidental areas and visible glyphs are exposure only, not interpreted.

features: The bottom row contains one continuous large specimen beside the red vessel.
A long fine green/brown shoot extends from the left junction horizontally across the row, then curves down the right side.
Several separate green triangular/arrow-like blades remain attached on the right-hand axis.
Two hanging elongated red/brown clusters of outlined small round units remain attached near the lower end.

The large horizontally oriented orange-brown swollen root has fine projecting fibres, tapers/curves at the right tip, and has alternating diagonal painted/unpainted bands. Paint bands are not interpreted as severed segments.

distinctive_concordance: Angular pointed basal-notched leaf silhouettes in both drawings.
Lax/arcing leafy axis ending in multiple red-centred clustered circular units.
Large orange-brown tapering root with fine peripheral fibres.
Leaf, cluster and root combination is more informative than colour alone, while still permitting stylized generic similarity.
counter_features: Herbal has tall upright main axis and many long side axes/cluster groups; pharmaceutical specimen has a single horizontal then descending shoot and two prominent terminal clusters.
Herbal root is one smoother asymmetric swelling; pharmaceutical root is much longer and has repeated diagonal colour/blank bands.
Relative size/axis orientation and leaf/cluster counts differ strongly; rotation/scaling alone is not enough to establish identical drawing anatomy.

continuity_or_cut.observed: Root-to-shoot junction and shoot-to-leaf/cluster paths are depicted as continuous. Fine tips taper or curve. No unequivocal detached cross-section or severing boundary identified.

simplification_rival: Abbreviated/reoriented depiction, altered emphasis of the swollen root, and fewer shoot branches explain the reduced page-scale arrangement without a securely different organ extent.

label_owner.geometry: One isolated inscription patch lies above the left root/shoot junction to the right of the vessel. Only one plant occurs in this complete bottom row; no explicit leader line is demonstrated. Glyph content and exact transcription locus are not verified.
other_possible_referents: The root rather than entire specimen remains a within-plant ownership alternative.
A row heading could reference the entire drawing; geometry alone does not exclude it.
The left red vessel has its own inscription patches; those are not silently treated as the plant label.

neighbor_alternatives.status: sole plant retained in full; no second bottom-row plant
red container retained as layout neighbor, not a plant identity rival

uncertainty: Compound visual similarity may support coidentity hypothesis, but changed root rendering is counterevidence.
The pharmaceutical drawing is visibly not root-only. A part relation based on absence of leaves is contradicted for this nominated specimen.
No claim that all organs shown equal a botanically complete living plant.
